questions.question: Find the smallest number to be added to 999, so that 99 divides the sum exactly.
questions.questionHtml: Find the smallest number to be added to 999, so that 99 divides the sum exactly.
questions.solution:
Given: Initial number = 999

Let x be the smallest number to be added

(999 + x) % 99 = 0, 999 % 99 = 9

x = 99 - 9 = 90

questions.question: In a circle, two chords MN and PQ intersect at O. If MO = 9 cm, ON = 5 cm and OQ = 6 cm, then the value of OP (in cm) is:
questions.questionHtml: In a circle, two chords MN and PQ intersect at O. If MO = 9 cm, ON = 5 cm and OQ = 6 cm, then the value of OP (in cm) is:
questions.solution:
Using the formula

MO × ON = OQ × OP:

⇒ 9 × 5 = 6 × OP

⇒ 45 = 6 × OP

⇒ OP = 7.5 cm

questions.question: In a △ABC right-angled at C, if tan A = √3, then the value of sin A cos B cot(A + B) is:
questions.questionHtml: In a △ABC right-angled at C, if tan A = √3, then the value of sin A cos B cot(A + B) is:
questions.solution:
tan A = √3, tan A = a/b = √3, a = √3b, c = √(a2 + b2) = 2b


sin A = a/c = √3/2, cos B = b/2b = 1/2, A + B = 90º, cot(90º) = 0

sin A × cos B × cot(A + B) = (√3/2) × (√3/2) × 0 = 0

questions.question: A rectangular courtyard is 4m 95cm long and 16m 65cm broad. It is to be paved with the square tiles of the same size. Find the least number of such square tiles required to pave the rectangular courtyard.
questions.questionHtml: A rectangular courtyard is 4m 95cm long and 16m 65cm broad. It is to be paved with the square tiles of the same size. Find the least number of such square tiles required to pave the rectangular courtyard.
questions.solution:
GCD of 495 and 1665 using Euclidean algorithm:

1665 ÷ 495 = 3 rem 180

495 ÷ 180 = 2 rem 135

180 ÷ 135 = 1 rem 45

135 ÷ 45 = 3 rem 0

GCD = 45 cm

Number of tiles = (495 × 1665) / (45 × 45) = 823575 / 2025 = 407

questions.question: There are two pipes to fill a tank. Together, they can fill the tank in 15 minutes. If one pipe can fill the tank in one and a half times as fast as the other, the faster pipe alone can fill the tank in:
questions.questionHtml: There are two pipes to fill a tank. Together, they can fill the tank in 15 minutes. If one pipe can fill the tank in one and a half times as fast as the other, the faster pipe alone can fill the tank in:
questions.solution:
Let the time taken by the faster pipe be x minutes.

Therefore, the time taken by the slower pipe will be 1.5x minutes.

(1/x) + (1/1.5x) = 1/15

(1/x) + (3/2x) = 1/15

(5/2x) = 1/15

5 × 15 = 2x, 75 = 2x, x = 37.5

Faster pipe: x/1.5 = 37.5/1.5 = 25 minutes

questions.question: Find the value of \(\frac{sec 35^{\circ}}{cosec 55^{\circ}} - \frac{cos 25^{\circ}}{sin 65^{\circ}}\)
questions.questionHtml:
Find the value of
\(\frac{sec 35^{\circ}}{cosec 55^{\circ}} - \frac{cos 25^{\circ}}{sin 65^{\circ}}\)
questions.solution:
Formula Used:

sec θ = 1 / cos θ, csc θ = 1 / sin θ

Calculation:

sec 35° / csc 55° = (1 / cos 35°) / (1 / sin 55°) = sin 55° / cos 35°

Since sin 55° = cos 35°, sin 55° / cos 35° = 1

Similarly, since sin 65° = cos 25°, cos 25° / sin 65° = cos 25° / cos 25° = 1

(1 - 1) = 0

questions.question: If the perimeter of an equilateral triangle is 36 units, then its area is (in square units):
questions.questionHtml: If the perimeter of an equilateral triangle is 36 units, then its area is (in square units):
questions.solution:
Side length = 36 / 3

Side length = 12 units

Area = (√3 / 4) × 122

Area = (√3 / 4) × 144

Area = 36√3 square units

questions.question: If a sin 3 X + b cos 3 X = sinX cosX and a sinX = b cosX, then find the value of a 2 + b 2 , provided that x is neither 0° nor 90°.
questions.questionHtml: If a sin<sup>3</sup>X + b cos<sup>3</sup>X = sinX cosX and a sinX = b cosX, then find the value of a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup>, provided that x is neither 0° nor 90°.
questions.solution:
a = (b cos X) / sin X

(b cos X) / sin X ×  sin3X + b cos3X = sin X cos X

b cos X (sin2X + cos2X) = sin X cos X

b cos X = sin X cos X

b = sin X

a = cos X

a2 + b2 = cos2X + sin2X

a2 + b2 = 1

questions.question: Atul gives Vishu a head-start of 20 seconds in a 900 m race and beats him by 135 m. While running the same race again Atul gives a start of 189 m and beats him by 8 seconds. In how much time can Vishu complete the full race of 900 m?

questions.solution:
765(Ta + 8) = 711(Ta + 20)

765Ta + 6120 = 711Ta + 14220 ,54Ta = 8100

Ta = 150 seconds

V = 765/170 = 4.5 m/s

Tv = 900/4.5

questions.question: The following pie chart shows the distribution of the percentage of students in various courses at the university. The total number of students (boys and girls only) in the university is 7000. In B.Com, there are 60% girls and in B.Sc. C.Sci, there are 40% boys. The total number of girls who took admission in B.Sc C.Sci and B.Com courses is what percentage of the total students admitted to the university?
questions.questionHtml:
The following pie chart shows the distribution of the percentage of students in various courses at the university. The total number of students (boys and girls only) in the university is 7000.

In B.Com, there are 60% girls and in B.Sc. C.Sci, there are 40% boys. The total number of girls who took admission in B.Sc C.Sci and B.Com courses is what percentage of the total students admitted to the university?
questions.solution:
Total number of students in the university = 7000.Total 

The total number of girls in B.Com and B.Sc. C.Sci are:

840 + 1050 = 1890

Percentage of girls = (Total number of girls / 7000) × 100

= (1890 / 7000) ×100 = 27 %

questions.question: In a division problem, the divisor is 4 times the quotient and 2 times the remainder. If the remainder is 32, then find the dividend.
questions.questionHtml: In a division problem, the divisor is 4 times the quotient and 2 times the remainder. If the remainder is 32, then find the dividend.
questions.solution:
Divisor = 2 × 32 = 64

64 = 4 × Quotient

Quotient = 64 / 4 = 16

Dividend = 64 × 16 + 32 = 1024 + 32 = 1056

questions.question: A group of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 62, and that of the rest is 62. What is the average score of the group?
questions.questionHtml: A group of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 62, and that of the rest is 62. What is the average score of the group?
questions.solution:
Total score of the group = (12 × 62) + (18 × 62)

Total number of students = 30

Total score of the group = 744 + 1116  = 1860

Average score of the group = 1860 / 30  = 62

questions.question: In a rhombus ABCD, O is any interior point such that OA = OC. What is five-ninths of the degree measure of ∠DOB?
questions.questionHtml: In a rhombus ABCD, O is any interior point such that OA = OC. What is five-ninths of the degree measure of ∠DOB?
questions.solution:
Given: OA = OC, O on bisector of AC

In rhombus, diagonals bisect at right angles

∠AOB = ∠COD = 90º

∠DOB = ∠AOB + ∠COD = 180º

Five-ninths of ∠DOB = (5/9) × 180º = 100º

questions.question: The bar graph below shows the production of coffee (in lakh tons) by four companies A, B, C and D over a period of four years from 2010 to 2013. Study the graph and answer the question that follows. The combined average production for four years of companies A and C is what percentage (rounded off to 2 decimal places) more/less than the combined average production for four years of companies B and D?
questions.questionHtml:
The bar graph below shows the production of coffee (in lakh tons) by four companies A, B, C and D over a period of four years from 2010 to 2013. Study the graph and answer the question that follows.

The combined average production for four years of companies A and C is what percentage (rounded off to 2 decimal places) more/less than the combined average production for four years of companies B and D?
questions.solution:
The combined average production for four years of

companies A and C is:

= (510 + 670)/8 = 147.5

The combined average production for four years of

companies B and D is:

= (530 + 750)/8 = 160

Percentage difference = ((Combined average of A and C - Combined average of B and D) / Combined average of B and D) * 100

= (147.8 - 160)/160 

= - 7.72 %

questions.question: Solve the given set of three equations to get the value of the unknowns: x + 2z = 3 x + 2y + 3z = 5 3x - 5z = -13
questions.questionHtml:
Solve the given set of three equations to get the value of the unknowns:
x + 2z = 3
x + 2y + 3z = 5
3x - 5z = -13
questions.solution:
x + 2z = 3, x = 3 - 2z

x + 2y + 3z = 5

(3 - 2z) + 2y + 3z = 5

3 + 2y + z = 5

2y + z = 2

y = (2 - z)/2

3x - 5z = -13

3(3 - 2z) - 5z = -13

9 - 11z = -13

-11z = -22, z = 2

x = 3 - 2(2) = -1

y = (2 - 2)/2 = 0

 x = -1, y = 0, z = 2

questions.question: Mrudula starts her job with a certain monthly salary and earns a fixed increment every year. If her salary was ₹28,400 after six years of service and ₹52,997 after fifteen years, find her annual increment.

questions.solution:

And, the salary of the Mrudula is ₹52,997 after 15 years.

Subtracting equation (1) from (2), we get

questions.question: A sum of money is divided among P, Q, R and S in the proportion of 4 : 9 : 2 : 3. If Q gets ₹560 more than R, then the share of S is:
questions.questionHtml: A sum of money is divided among P, Q, R and S in the proportion of 4 : 9 : 2 : 3. If Q gets ₹560 more than R, then the share of S is:
questions.solution:
Let shares be 4x, 9x, 2x, 3x.

9x - 2x = 560

7x = 560, x = 80

Share of S = 3x = 3 × 80 = ₹240

questions.question: Study the given table and answer the question that follows. The given table shows the number of candidates who appeared (both male and female) in a Public Examination and the percentage of those who qualified in the examination from two states X and Z. Few values are missing in the table (indicated by ------). You will be required to fill them according to the question. Year State X: Number of appeared candidates State X: Percentage of qualified candidates State Z: Number of appeared candidates State Z: Percentage of qualified candidates 2008 480 70% -------- 70% 2009 560 75% 500 80% 2010 -------- 60% 650 50% 2011 450 89% 720 72% 2012 790 -------- 660 -------- Out of the number of qualified candidates from State X in 2010, the ratio of male to female candidates is 5 : 7. If the number of female qualified candidates from State X in 2010 is 168, what is the number of appeared candidates (both male and female) from State X in 2010?
questions.questionHtml:
Study the given table and answer the question that follows.
The given table shows the number of candidates who appeared (both male and female) in a Public Examination and the percentage of those who qualified in the examination from two states X and Z. Few values are missing in the table (indicated by ------). You will be required to fill them according to the question.
Year State X: Number of appeared candidates State X: Percentage of qualified candidates State Z: Number of appeared candidates State Z: Percentage of qualified candidates
2008 480 70% -------- 70%
2009 560 75% 500 80%
2010 -------- 60% 650 50%
2011 450 89% 720 72%
2012 790 -------- 660 --------

Out of the number of qualified candidates from State X in 2010, the ratio of male to female candidates is 5 : 7. If the number of female qualified candidates from State X in 2010 is 168, what is the number of appeared candidates (both male and female) from State X in 2010?
questions.solution:
The total number of qualified candidates from State X in 2010 is 288. Since 60% of the appeared candidates qualify

we can write:

\(\dfrac{60}{100} \times \text{Total appeared candidates} = 288\)

⇒ \(\text{Total appeared candidates} = \frac{288× 100}{60} \)

⇒ \(\text{Total appeared candidates} = 480\)

questions.question: A shopkeeper, on the eve of Diwali, allowed a series of discounts on television sets. Find the selling price of a television set, if the marked price of television is ₹1,200 and successive discounts are 15% and 10%.
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper, on the eve of Diwali, allowed a series of discounts on television sets. Find the selling price of a television set, if the marked price of television is ₹1,200 and successive discounts are 15% and 10%.
questions.solution:
Marked price = ₹1,200

Successive discounts = 15% and 10%

Selling Price = ₹1,200 × 0.85 × 0.90 = ₹918
